drivingQuestion: How is the 'one day' of the prohibition of an animal and its offspring reckoned?
outcomeNote: A mishna stating a rule together with its scriptural derivation; nothing is contested here.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ הָאָמוּר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ – הַיּוֹם הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַלַּיְלָה. אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא: נֶאֱמַר בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית ״יוֹם אֶחָד״, וְנֶאֱמַר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ – מָה ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ הָאָמוּר בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית הַיּוֹם הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַלַּיְלָה, אַף ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ הָאָמוּר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ הַיּוֹם הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַלַּיְלָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to the phrase «“one day” that is stated with regard to» the prohibition against slaughtering an animal «itself and its offspring, the day follows the night.» Therefore, one may slaughter an animal during the day and slaughter its offspring that night, but one may not slaughter an animal at night and slaughter its offspring the following day. «Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma derived this» by means of a verbal analogy. «It is stated in the act of Creation: “One day”» (Genesis 1:5), «and it is stated with regard to» the slaughter of an animal «itself and its offspring: “One day”» (Leviticus 22:28). «Just as» concerning the phrase «“one day” that is stated in the act of Creation, the day follows the night, so too» concerning the phrase «“one day” that is stated with regard to» the slaughter of an animal «itself and its offspring, the day follows the night.»

moves.summary: the mishna rules that the day is reckoned as following the night
moves.about: attributing to ben Zoma the verbal analogy that fixes the day of the prohibition as running from morning to night

moves.cueHe: את זו דרש רבי שמעון בן זומא
moves.summary: ben Zoma proves the ruling by a verbal analogy from the Creation account
moves.about: bringing the 'one day' of the Creation account as the anchor term of the verbal analogy
